question: Does a second clean builder produce the same dist/ and the same tarball as the final candidate?

method.source: git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <copy> for each copy
method.isolation: Each copy got its own HOME, npm_config_cache, and TMPDIR under its own directory.
method.comparison: dist/index.js SHA-256, sorted dist/ path+hash digest, tarball SHA-256, tarball file content digest, file counts

finding.reading: Two independent clean copies, each with a fresh HOME and cache, produced byte-identical tarballs and identical dist/ content. The local npm pack also produced the same raw tarball SHA-256.

result: B1: dist and tarball both match across two clean builders.
limits: Both builders ran on the same machine and toolchain; this is not a cross-machine reproducibility claim.
The tarball contains only dist, README, LICENSE, CREDITS, and CHANGELOG; docs/ and scripts/ are not packaged.
No publish, stage, tag, or approval was performed.
